summary:
The slice adds one test and changes no src. The test is TopLevelTests.AnInPlaceCorrectionOfARootLevelFileNameMarksThatFileRowRevised (TopLevelTests.cs:121-147). It does what it is meant to, and it guards the file-row half of the Revised latch.

Run on this tree:
- **Whole default suite:** 936/936, exit 0, 29 s.
- **TopLevel filter:** exit 0, new Fact passed.
- **New Fact alone:** 15/15 repeats passed.
- **The committed Mutants.ps1:** exit 0 in 50 s. Unmutated, 25/25 under both temp folders. Under mutant A (`r.Kind != EntryKind.File &&` at TopLevelTracker.cs:194), 25 tests ran and exactly the new Fact went red, with 'row a-stale.bin: Revised is False', under both temps. src hashes were unchanged, `git diff src` was 0, and no fsa-sl105-* copy was left behind.
- **Architecture rules (Fitness):** 92 rules, all hold.
- **ScratchRootCorpus.Tests.ps1:** all 11 rows held. It orphaned one ping.exe, as the already-filed SC-327 says; I stopped it.
- **Windows Sandbox (fresh Windows 11 build 26100.9457, at defaults, ordinary medium-integrity user):** the Fact passed 10/10, so the stale-entry fixture held off this PC too. The TopLevel filter there was 23/25; the 2 failures are the existing symlink tests failing with error 1314 because Developer Mode is off in the Sandbox (Q-001), which this slice did not touch.
- **First Sandbox attempt:** run as SYSTEM, it was invalid. SYSTEM's temp path is forced to C:\Windows\SystemTemp whatever TEMP says, and TempTree refuses to build a tree there by design.

**Criteria:** 1-9 and 11 are met. Criterion 10 (a File row corrected in OnDisk only, or Bytes only) was not driven. The design ruled it not material, and the latch compares the (Bytes, OnDisk) pair with no branch on which figure moved.

**Not reached:**
- Windows 10 (O-009): no machine here, and the Sandbox is Windows 11.
- A stale hardlink on a real drive scanned by the shipped exe.

**Assumption:** the bug report was title-only. I took its meaning from the investigation: a missing positive test, with the behaviour already correct.

criteria.criterion: 1. recognise that the suite guards the file-row latch — when the default suite contains one Fact with a root-level hardlink name, an Append through another name, a Watch scan, a File-row marker and a literal-true Revised assertion
criteria.how: Read TopLevelTests.cs:121-147. It has TempTree.Hardlink(tree.PathOf("a-stale.bin"), current) at :127, TempTree.Append(current, 63 * MiB) at :128, Watch(tree.Root, correctedRows: ["a-stale.bin"]) at :130, EntryKind.File, and the literal-true tuple at :143. The Fact has no Trait, so it runs in the default suite (936/936 here). The repro command's exit 0 is the engine's own measurement (O-001); I did not re-run it, per the rules.

criteria.criterion: 2. mark a probe-corrected top-level row Revised — when the row is a FILE directly under the scan root, a second hardlink name whose root-listing size is stale because the file grew through a name in a subfolder
criteria.how: The Fact asserts the final row is (File, Done, 64 MiB, Revised true), with OnDisk equal to the store's (:143-144). It passed in the full suite (936/936), the TopLevel filter (exit 0), 15/15 isolated repeats on this PC, and 10/10 runs in a fresh Windows 11 26100.9457 Sandbox as an ordinary user.

criteria.criterion: 3. show a top-level file row at seed — when the first snapshot, before the probe pass: the root-level File row is Done at the stale 1 MiB and not Revised
criteria.how: The assert at :136 comes right after the Completed assert and requires Snapshots[0] a-stale.bin to be (File, Done, 1 MiB, false). It passed in every run above (26 isolated runs over two machines plus the suite), so the entry was still stale at Seed each time.

criteria.criterion: 4. credit an in-place correction to the right row — when the name the write went through lies inside a subfolder row ('sub') that is not the corrected row
criteria.how: The assert at :146 requires sub to be (Done, 0, Files 1, Folders 1, Revised false). correctedRows holds only a-stale.bin, so the watcher's `(corrected || !row.Revised)` check (TopLevelTests.cs:707) also holds sub unrevised in every snapshot. It passed in all runs.

criteria.criterion: 5. the guard dies with the defect it guards — when the Revised latch is gated by row kind: `r.Kind != EntryKind.File &&` in TopLevelTracker.Build's latch
criteria.how: Ran `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/bugs/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard/Mutants.ps1`: exit 0. The old text was found exactly once, Core.dll was written after the edit, and 25 tests ran, as many as unmutated. Exactly the new Fact went red, with the message 'row a-stale.bin: Revised is False', under both the Engine and the Ordinary temp. The worktree src hash was unchanged and `git diff --exit-code src` returned 0.

criteria.criterion: 6. run under the engine's temp folder — when TEMP and TMP point at C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, as when the engine runs validate
criteria.how: Mutants.ps1's Engine arm (TEMP and TMP set to %SystemRoot%\TEMP) passed 25/25 unmutated and killed only the new Fact under mutant A.

criteria.criterion: 7. run inside the whole default suite — when the Fact runs alongside every other test collection in parallel, under the default VSTestTestCaseFilter
criteria.how: `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx`: 'Passed! - Failed: 0, Passed: 936, Total: 936, Duration: 26 s', exit 0, 29 s wall. The build-check recorded 935 before the slice.

criteria.criterion: 8. mark a corrected top-level row Revised — when the root-level row is a LINK (junction or symlink), which Seed also settles
criteria.how: The design marked this case not material, and its reason holds on the tree. Build maps a Link row to NotFollowed (TopLevelTracker.cs:188), and the latch requires Done (:194), so a Link row can never be marked Revised and no mark is owed. The watcher asserts `!row.Revised || row.State == Done` for every row in every Watch scan (TopLevelTests.cs:681). TopLevelLinksAreNotFollowedRowsWithNothingCounted passed in the 936/936 run. Nothing needed building.

criteria.criterion: 9. never mark an uncorrected top-level file row — when a root-level file whose listing is current, so no probe correction reaches it
criteria.how: The design marked this not material. The watcher's `(corrected || !row.Revised)` (:707) and 'revised in the snapshot it settled in' (:712) checks apply to every root-level File row in every Watch-based Fact, and all of them passed in the 936/936 run. Nothing needed building.

criteria.criterion: 10. mark a corrected top-level file row Revised — when the correction moves only OnDisk, or only Bytes, for a File row
criteria.how: No test or run of mine drove a File row whose correction moves only one figure. The design ruled it not material, so no test was owed: the latch (:194) compares the (Bytes, OnDisk) pair and has no branch on kind beyond Done. ACorrectionOfADoneRowMarksItOnlyWhenAFigureMoved, which pins the which-figure branch over folder rows, passed in the suite. That this holds for a File row is a reading of the code, not a measurement.

criteria.criterion: 11. keep the fixture stale until the scan — when something opens a-stale.bin by name between the Append and Watch
criteria.how: The Fact body (:124-130) does nothing to a-stale.bin between the Append and Watch. If anything had refreshed the entry, the snapshot-0 assert at :136 would fail by name. It passed in 15/15 isolated runs and the full suite on this PC, and in 10/10 runs on a fresh Sandbox. Defender was not running in the Sandbox, so Defender opening the name was exercised only on this PC, where its state I did not read.

obligations.evidence: No Windows 10 machine exists here (already open under Q-192/Q-224), so this cannot be measured on this machine. The Sandbox is Windows 11: its registry ProductName reads 'Windows 10 Enterprise', a known registry quirk, but its build is 26100.9457 (24H2). What I did measure off this PC: the Fact passed 10/10 in a fresh Windows 11 26100.9457 Sandbox as an ordinary medium-integrity user. That includes the snapshot-0 assert, so NTFS per-name staleness held on a second Windows 11 build at defaults. Windows 10 itself was not reached.
